memory_candidates.content: In this codebase's bash+jq scripts, never use `${var:-{}}` as a jq-input default (e.g. `jq ... <<< "${var:-{}}"`). Bash's parameter-expansion parser mishandles a literal `{}` default: when `var` is non-empty it silently appends a stray trailing `}` to the expansion (confirmed via `bash -c 'x=hello; echo "${x:-{}}"'` -> `hello}`), corrupting the value with no error. Use `${var:-null}` instead — jq's `//` operators (`.field // 0`, `.field // []`) handle a `null` input cleanly, and the bash expansion has no such quirk.

When embedding a jq program inside a bash single-quoted string (the `"$SOME_JQ_DEFS"'...'` splice idiom used throughout agent-system/extensions/core/scripts), never write an apostrophe (possessive 's, contractions) inside a bash `#`-comment within that jq block. The apostrophe is parsed as a literal single-quote by BASH (not jq) at that point, prematurely terminating the enclosing single-quoted string and producing a bash syntax error several lines later, far from the actual apostrophe. Existing spliced jq blocks in this codebase (Class A/B in orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh, Check 8/9 in validate-state.sh) are already deliberately apostrophe-free in their comments for this reason.

Sourcing lib/file-scope-overlap.sh (or any lib using the `read -r -d '' VAR <<'EOF' ... EOF` heredoc-into-variable idiom) from a script running `set -euo pipefail` must NEVER use a bare `. lib.sh` or `source lib.sh`. `read -d ''` always returns a non-zero exit status at the heredoc's end (no NUL delimiter is ever found), which aborts the whole script under `-e` the instant it is sourced. The established idiom in this codebase (orchestrate-batch-admit.sh, task-lock.sh) wraps the sourcing in a tested `if ! . "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh" 2>/dev/null; then echo ERROR...; exit 2; fi` — the `if` test makes the command's exit status -e-exempt. Scripts using `set -uo pipefail` (no `-e`), like validate-state.sh, don't need this wrapper and can source plainly.
